statement: Thailand long-stay/remote-work visa options (incl. DTV) and entry requirements are set by Thai authorities; applications and rules are handled via the official e-visa/arrival systems.
The Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa criteria and benefits are defined by the Thailand Board of Investment.
Thai tax residency is based on physical presence and foreign-income treatment is administered by the Thai Revenue Department; rules and their application change and are not advice.
Whether a foreigner can open a Thai bank account depends on visa type and each bank's current KYC policy; banks publish their own terms.
Retirement-route (50+) financial requirements and O/O-A processes are defined by Thai immigration/consular authorities and vary by post.
Insurance required for certain long-stay/retirement visas must meet regulator criteria; the Office of Insurance Commission and the long-stay insurer list are the official references.
Thailand operates a digital arrival card (TDAC) completed before entry via the immigration portal.
Thailand has an address-notification requirement (TM30) handled by the host/landlord/immigration.
Certain long-stay holders must report their address every 90 days (TM47) via the immigration portal.
Thai SIM/eSIM registration requires passport ID verification under NBTC rules; AIS and True/dtac are the main mobile operators.
Bangkok has BTS Skytrain and MRT underground metro services with stored-value cards.
An Airport Rail Link connects Suvarnabhumi (BKK) airport to the city rail network.
Ride-hailing (e.g., Grab) and LINE (dominant messaging) apps are widely used in Bangkok for transport and everyday services.
Thailand's national emergency/medical assistance numbers exist (e.g., medical emergency 1669); tourist police provide English assistance.
Bangkok has numerous internationally accredited private hospitals offering English-speaking care and often insurer direct billing.
Crowd-sourced cost-of-living indices (Numbeo/LivingCost) exist for Bangkok and are usable only as directional cross-checks, not quotes.
The Bank of Thailand publishes official daily FX (THB) reference rates for currency conversion.
Official real-time air-quality (AQI/PM2.5) data for Bangkok is published by the Pollution Control Department (Air4Thai).
The International Schools Association of Thailand (ISAT) maintains a directory of member international schools; fees are set per school.
Mobile operators market tourist SIM and eSIM plans with varying data/price; specific prices must be checked at purchase.
Home fixed broadband plans in Thailand are offered by major telecoms; speed/price to be confirmed per address/operator.
Licensed cross-border money-transfer services (e.g., Wise/DeeMoney) exist for moving funds; fees and eligibility vary.
A possible shortening of visa-exempt entry length has been reported by secondary media but is NOT officially confirmed.
Bangkok has multiple coworking spaces; availability, Wi-Fi quality and rates must be verified per venue.
